thread:
ashok: Quick heads up — ran long-context (~16k tokens) prefill experiments with INT8 kernels after the new calibration pass and saw prefill TTFT and decode behavior diverge vs FP8. TL;DR: prefill TTFT regressed ~2x, steady-state decode latency up ~25-35% depending on turn size. Anyone else hit this after the int8 calibration change?

maria: Which calibration change specifically? per-tensor affine -> per-channel?

ashok: per-tensor fallback from the int8 calibration pipeline (we had a conservative fallback for some layers). Repro configs below.

ashok: ```bash
# baseline (FP8)
model: mix-fp8
ctx: 16384
batch: 1
TTFT: 120ms
TPS: ~42

# int8-calib (current)
model: int8-fallback
ctx: 16384
batch: 1
TTFT: 280ms
TPS: ~18
```

kevin: Those TTFT deltas smell like kernel selection falling back to a non-optimized matmul for large seq lengths. Did you capture kernel names from the selector trace?

ashok: Yep — kernel_selector.log shows a fallback to generic_gemm_int8 for the prefill giant matmuls (shape ~[seq, hidden]). KV cache warm path uses a different, smaller-kernel layout and looks fine. The big hit is the prefill matmul implementation not vectorizing for int8 blocked sizes. Kernel 0x7f9 accounts for ~86% of prefill time in the trace.

olivia: Could be the packing overhead + dequant path. Have you tried packing multiple requests (larger continuous-batching) to amortize the pack/unpack?

ashok: I tried pack=4 (pack short sequences together) — prefill TTFT dropped from 280ms -> 190ms, so batching helps the prefill stage. But decode (turn-by-turn) still regresses on small batches: dequant + reorder overhead shows up per token.

perf-bot: perf/regression detected: prefill_ttft +58% (int8-calib vs fp8-baseline) on commit abc123. Dashboard: https://perf.redwood/internal/regs/1792345678

kevin: Also double-check KV cache layout. If keys/values are stored as int8 and dequant happens during decode, that moves cost into the hot path. Perhaps keep KV in fp16 while using int8 for prefill? That would be a hybrid approach.

maria: Good point — dequanting at every decode step will kill short-turn latency. Can you dump the op-level breakdown (dequant, reorder, matmul) for a 4-token decode run?

ashok: Will run microbench. Plan: (1) single-matmul microbench for shapes [seq=4096, hidden=4096], [seq=8192, hidden=4096] across fp16/fp8/int8, capture kernel names and time; (2) harness prefill+N decode tokens to see split; (3) try hybrid: prefill in fp8 or fp16, KV stored fp16, decode in int8 if possible.

olivia: Also add a short-term rule to kernel selector: if seq_len > threshold AND quantized path selects a non-vectorized fallback, prefer fp8/vectorized kernel for prefill. That keeps steady-state cost lower. We can later tune quality/quant tradeoffs.

kevin: If fallback is coming from calibration stats (e.g., per-tensor not matching ranges), we should also try per-channel calibration for problematic layers — lower residuals, might enable the optimized int8 GEMM. But that's more calibration work.

ashok: Running microbench on a100 + p4x tonight. I'll post kernel trace + flamegraph. Also will try the hybrid KV layout to measure decode token tail.

maria: Thanks. If you can attach the kernel_selector.log and the perf flamegraph link we can triage faster.

ashok: Filed a short ticket and attached traces: https://redwood.internal/trace/1792345678 — will update with microbench numbers in this thread.

maria: :thumbsup: Let's sync tomorrow after results.
